authors: Renjini Lalitha, Matthew Hicks, Mosarrat Qureshi, Kumar Kumaran
summary: This study investigates risk factors for Bell's Stage III necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC-III) in preterm neonates born <33 weeks gestation, focusing on the association between umbilical arterial catheter (UAC) duration and NEC-III development. It found that UAC duration >5 days and earlier onset distinguish NEC-III from NEC-II.
methods:
• Single-center retrospective case-control study, 2015-2018
• Neonates <33 weeks GA, 1360 admissions
• Cases: NEC-III; Controls: NEC-II (1:1) and non-NEC (1:2–4) matched by GA ±1 week and birth date ±3 months
• Data sources: neonatal database and chart review
• Variables: maternal/neonatal demographics, perinatal data, feeding, UAC presence/duration, illness severity (SNAPPE-II)
• Statistics: χ², Fisher’s, ANOVA/t-tests; multivariate logistic regression (p<0.2 entry, p<0.05 significance)
findings:
• NEC-III incidence 46% of NEC cases; median onset 13.7 vs 23.9 days (NEC-II), p=0.01
• Lower GA in NEC-III (25.4±2.3 vs 27.3±2.7 weeks), p=0.0003
• Higher illness severity: SNAPPE-II 47.5 vs 28.4 (NEC-II) and 37 (non-NEC), p=0.003
• UAC >5 days independently associated with NEC-III (AOR provided in full paper)
• Suggests upper limit for UAC duration may prevent NEC-III
